# Code for Sander
Hi Sander,

What I would like to do is try to visualize the data stratified by metrics of instability. For example, IPH <10% vs IPH > 10%. This may be horrible, but I think its worth a try. You did this nicely in your NatCVR paper but separated instead by plaque cluster. 

I think we should define the metrics as "associated with stability" or "instability". e.g., those <10% SMC would be associated with instability; >10% with stability. for lipid and IPH >10% = instability. We can then label the groups this way

Data should be binned as per your analysis for IPH, Lipid and SMC content. 

In terms of specific genes to look at, based on your first look the most interesting would be:

CD3E
GZMB
RUNX3
PRDM1
ZAP70
GNLY

## Violin Plot Approach
```{r}
# Generate test dataset
data <- data.frame(
  Gene = rep(c("CD3E", "GZMB", "RUNX3", "PRDM1", "ZAP70", "GNLY"), each = 300), # 3 genes, 300 rows each (100 per condition)
  Condition = rep(c("IPH Content", "Fat Content", "SMC Content"), each = 100, times = 3), # 3 conditions per gene
  Group = rep(rep(c("Stable", "Unstable"), each = 50), times = 9), # High and Low for each condition
  expression = c(
    rnorm(50, mean = 0.25, sd = 0.06), rnorm(50, mean = 0.4, sd = 0.05),  # Gene1
    rnorm(50, mean = 0.45, sd = 0.05), rnorm(50, mean = 0.6, sd = 0.07),   # Gene2
    rnorm(50, mean = 0.6, sd = 0.03), rnorm(50, mean = 0.5, sd = 0.04),   # Gene3
    
    rnorm(50, mean = 0.2, sd = 0.06), rnorm(50, mean = 0.5, sd = 0.05),  # Gene1
    rnorm(50, mean = 0.28, sd = 0.05), rnorm(50, mean = 0.55, sd = 0.07), # Gene2
    rnorm(50, mean = 0.9, sd = 0.03), rnorm(50, mean = 0.38, sd = 0.04),  # Gene 3
    
    rnorm(50, mean = 0.24, sd = 0.05), rnorm(50, mean = 0.83, sd = 0.06), # Gene1
    rnorm(50, mean = 0.62, sd = 0.07), rnorm(50, mean = 0.92, sd = 0.05), # Gene2
    rnorm(50, mean = 0.42, sd = 0.04), rnorm(50, mean = 0.42, sd = 0.03),  # Gene3
     rnorm(50, mean = 0.25, sd = 0.06), rnorm(50, mean = 0.4, sd = 0.05),  # Gene1
    rnorm(50, mean = 0.45, sd = 0.05), rnorm(50, mean = 0.6, sd = 0.07),   # Gene2
    rnorm(50, mean = 0.6, sd = 0.03), rnorm(50, mean = 0.5, sd = 0.04),   # Gene3
    
    rnorm(50, mean = 0.2, sd = 0.06), rnorm(50, mean = 0.5, sd = 0.05),  # Gene1
    rnorm(50, mean = 0.28, sd = 0.05), rnorm(50, mean = 0.55, sd = 0.07), # Gene2
    rnorm(50, mean = 0.9, sd = 0.03), rnorm(50, mean = 0.38, sd = 0.04),  # Gene 3
    
    rnorm(50, mean = 0.24, sd = 0.05), rnorm(50, mean = 0.83, sd = 0.06), # Gene1
    rnorm(50, mean = 0.62, sd = 0.07), rnorm(50, mean = 0.92, sd = 0.05), # Gene2
    rnorm(50, mean = 0.42, sd = 0.04), rnorm(50, mean = 0.42, sd = 0.03)  # Gene3
  )
)


data$Group <- factor(data$Group, levels = c("Stable", "Unstable"))


# Define colors for groups
col <- list(
  Group = c("Stable" = "#00C7CC", "Unstable" = "#FA7F74")
)
```

```{r, fig.height=30, fig.width=10}
plots <- list()


for (gene in unique(data$Gene)) {
  for (condition in unique(data$Condition)) {
 
    subset_data <- subset(data, Gene == gene & Condition == condition)

    p <- ggplot(subset_data, aes(x = Group, y = expression, fill = Group)) +
      geom_violin(trim = FALSE, scale = "width") +
      geom_jitter(shape = 16, position = position_jitter(width = 0.2), size = 1, color = "black") + 
      geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, outlier.shape = NA) + 
      scale_fill_manual(values = col$Group) +         # Use color mapping
      theme_pubr() +
      labs(y = paste0(gene, " Expression"), x = "", title = paste(condition)) +
      theme(
        aspect.ratio = 1,
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 15),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 15),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 15),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 20),
        legend.position = "none"                      # Remove legend
      )
    
    plots[[paste(gene, condition, sep = "_")]] <- p
  }
}


# Arrange plots in a grid
plot_grid(
  plotlist = plots,        # Use the list of plots
  ncol = 3,                # Arrange in 3 columns
  align = "v",             # Align vertically
  axis = "tb"              # Align top and bottom axes
)

```

## Heatmap Approach
### IPH
```{r}
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

data$ID <- rep(1:100, 18)


hm_list <- list()

for (condition in unique(data$Condition)) {
  
Heatmap_Genes <- subset(data, data$Condition == condition)
mtx <- Heatmap_Genes
mtx$Group <- NULL
mtx <- mtx %>% pivot_wider(names_from = ID, values_from = expression)
mtx$Gene <- NULL
mtx$Condition <- NULL
mtx <- as.matrix(mtx)

meta <- Heatmap_Genes[1:100, ]
meta$Condition <- factor(meta$Condition, levels = c("Stable", "Unstable"))

cluster_anno <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  cluster = meta$Group,
  show_annotation_name = FALSE,
  annotation_label = FALSE,
  annotation_name_rot = 5,
  show_legend = FALSE,
  annotation_legend_param = list(labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 0)),
  col = list(cluster = col$Group))

gene <- unique(data$Gene)

# Create the row annotation for genes
gene_anno <- rowAnnotation(
  Gene = anno_text(gene, rot = 0, gp = gpar(fontsize = 10)))

# Set up heatmap colors and legend
col_fun <- colorRamp2(c(0, 0.25, 0.75), c("blue", "#EEEEEE", "red"))
heatmap_legend_params <- list(
  legend_direction = "vertical",
  legend_width = unit(3, "cm"),
  labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 15),
  labels_rot = -90,
  title = "",
  title_gp = gpar(box_fill = "grey"),
  at = c(0, 0.25, 0.75)
)

# Draw heatmap

hm_list[[condition]] <- Heatmap(
  mtx,
  top_annotation = cluster_anno,
  left_annotation = gene_anno,
  height = nrow(mtx)*unit(5, "mm"),
  width = ncol(mtx)*unit(0.5, "mm"),
  border = TRUE,
  row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 5),
  col = col_fun,
  cluster_rows = F,
  cluster_columns = F,
  show_row_dend = FALSE,
  cluster_row_slices = FALSE,
  show_column_names = FALSE,
  cluster_column_slices = FALSE,
  column_names_side = NULL,
  row_title = " ",
  column_title = condition,
  heatmap_legend_param = heatmap_legend_params
)


}


hm_list
```
